requirement:
Pass a file-root address to obtain its selectable nodes. The tool accepts an address on the first call as well as one obtained from a listing.

```text
outline_source(NodeAddress) -> {node: NodeId, items: {node: NodeId, file: string, selector: string, kind: string}[], next?: UUID}
```
rationale:
structural: No clause of `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.outline_source.mcp` fixes how the tool is built. Each clause describes what an MCP client can observe.

- "Pass a file-root address to obtain its selectable nodes." This is input-to-output behavior of the tool.
- "The tool accepts an address on the first call as well as one obtained from a listing." This is about which inputs are accepted. Any implementation could meet it, whether it resolves the address through a cache or by parsing it directly. It names no library, algorithm, type or delegation.
- The `text` signature block, `outline_source(NodeAddress) -> {node, items:{node,file,selector,kind}[], next?}`, gives the tool's request and response shape on the wire. A different Rust declaration, such as other struct names, a helper type or a hand-built JSON value, would produce the same MCP request and response and still satisfy the text. So the Rust types are discretionary. Only the serialized shape is required, and tests can check that.

The review roots are empty. The requirement has no implementation edges. It has three test edges, which supply the evidence for the behavioral obligations. No structural obligation needs implementation evidence, so there is no gap.

behavioral: The requirement's observable obligations are: (a) `outline_source` accepts a file-root address on the first call, without a prior listing; (b) it also accepts an address obtained from a listing; (c) the result has the shape `{node, items:[{node,file,selector,kind}], next?}`. The reviewed tests cover each.

(a) First-call addresses:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[edge_and_outline_tools_accept_source_addresses_and_domain_data]` calls `outline_source` as the model's first outline call. It passes `{path, location:""}` and then `{data:{id:8}}`.
- It asserts the full response is `{node, items:[{node, file:"alpha.txt", selector:"", kind:""}]}`.
- It also checks the tool schema for `outline_source`: `node` is an integer and `data` references a schema whose `id` is an integer.
- `project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outline_continuations_keep_the_file_and_complete_ordered_items]` calls `outline_source` with `{path:"code.rs"}` and with `{node: <interned node>}`. It asserts both give the same items.

(b) Listing-obtained addresses:
- `project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outline_tool_rejects_excluded_and_unreadable_sources_without_domain_reads]` takes the `files[index]` reference from a `list_sources` result and passes it to `outline_source`. This is done for `source.txt` and for `invalid.rs`.
- It asserts `outline["node"] == reference["node"]`, that `items[0].node` is a number, and that the outline has three items for `source.txt`.

(c) Result shape:
- The continuation test checks every item's `node`, `file`, `selector` and `kind` against the expected values: `fn` kind, `fn[item_N]` selectors and file `code.rs`.
- It follows `next` through multiple pages. It checks that each page's `node` is the file root, that the pages concatenate to all 401 items in order, and that `pages > 1`.
- The `next` field is absent on the last page.

Together these tests assert each obligation and the output form, so I found no gap.
